description: 7-layer AIOS framework definition and assessment criteria

layers.name: Stack
layers.description: The tools the business already uses — CRM, billing, PM, email, calendar, ERP. We assess API readiness, data portability, and MCP availability. Connect-first philosophy: keep what works.

assessment_criteria.score_1_3: Mostly closed/legacy tools with no APIs, data trapped in proprietary formats
assessment_criteria.score_4_6: Mix of modern and legacy tools, some have APIs but not consistently used
assessment_criteria.score_7_10: Modern stack with REST/GraphQL APIs, data accessible, tools chosen for openness

key_questions: What tools do you use daily?
Can you export your data from each tool?
Do your tools have APIs or integration options?

layers.name: Connections
layers.description: MCP servers, native APIs, webhooks, automation platforms (Make/n8n) that wire tools together. The nervous system of the AIOS.

assessment_criteria.score_1_3: Tools are siloed, data manually copied between systems, no automations
assessment_criteria.score_4_6: Some Zapier/Make automations, a few native integrations, but gaps remain
assessment_criteria.score_7_10: Most tools connected via MCP or APIs, data flows automatically, webhooks for real-time sync

key_questions: Which tools currently talk to each other?
Do you manually transfer data between tools?
Do you use any automation platforms (Zapier, Make, n8n)?

layers.name: Intelligence
layers.description: Claude Code is the builder — creates integrations, writes MCP connections, deploys agents, builds skills. Claude Cowork is the operator — handles web tasks, browser automation, computer use, real-time agentic work. Together they form the intelligence hub. Make/n8n/Zapier sit alongside for scheduled orchestration.

assessment_criteria.score_1_3: No AI tools in use, or only basic ChatGPT for ad-hoc questions
assessment_criteria.score_4_6: Using Claude/ChatGPT for content, some exploration of automation, no systematic AI integration
assessment_criteria.score_7_10: Claude Code actively building integrations, Cowork running operations, AI embedded in daily workflows

key_questions: How do you currently use AI in your business?
Have you tried Claude Code or similar developer tools?
Do you have any AI-powered automations running?

layers.name: Data OS
layers.description: All tool data accessible, structured, queryable. A single source of truth the AI layer can query: client records, financial data, project status, communications. Could be Supabase, Notion, Airtable, or custom DB.

assessment_criteria.score_1_3: Data scattered across tools with no centralization, can't answer basic cross-tool questions
assessment_criteria.score_4_6: Some data centralized (e.g., CRM as hub), but many silos remain, manual reporting
assessment_criteria.score_7_10: Single source of truth accessible to AI, cross-tool queries possible, automated data sync

key_questions: Where does your most important business data live?
Can you easily get a 360-degree view of a client?
How do you generate business reports — manually or automated?

layers.name: Skills
layers.description: Custom Claude Code skills (slash commands) for business processes. Each skill encodes a workflow: /onboard-client, /generate-invoice, /prep-meeting, /analyze-competitor. These are the business's institutional knowledge made executable.

assessment_criteria.score_1_3: No custom skills or automation scripts, all processes manual
assessment_criteria.score_4_6: Some scripts or macros, maybe a few Make/Zapier workflows, but not systematic
assessment_criteria.score_7_10: Library of Claude Code skills encoding key business processes, team actively creates and refines skills

key_questions: What are your most repetitive business processes?
Do you have any documented SOPs that could be automated?
How do you onboard new team members on processes?

layers.name: Context OS
layers.description: The business's identity layer that makes AI personal and reliable: CLAUDE.md equivalent with business rules, brand voice, decision frameworks. Memory files with client preferences, project history. Goal tracking, process documentation, team profiles.

assessment_criteria.score_1_3: No documented context, AI gives generic responses, institutional knowledge lives in people's heads
assessment_criteria.score_4_6: Some documentation exists (brand guide, SOPs), but not in a format AI can use
assessment_criteria.score_7_10: Rich Context OS with CLAUDE.md, client memory, process docs — AI produces work indistinguishable from the business

key_questions: Is your brand voice documented?
Do you have SOPs for your key processes?
If you left the business for a month, could someone follow your processes from docs alone?

layers.name: Dashboard
layers.description: A centralized command center to manage the AIOS. Could be a Notion workspace, custom web app, or Claude Code project structure. Shows active automations, data flows, recent AI actions, pending reviews, skill library, context health.

assessment_criteria.score_1_3: No central view, switching between many tools to understand business state
assessment_criteria.score_4_6: Some dashboards in individual tools, maybe a Notion page, but no unified view
assessment_criteria.score_7_10: Single pane of glass showing all AIOS activity, health metrics, and actionable insights

key_questions: How do you check on the overall state of your business?
Do you have a dashboard or reporting hub?
How many tools do you check daily to stay informed?

maturity_levels.name: Disconnected
maturity_levels.description: Tools exist but don't talk to each other. Data manually transferred. No AI integration.

maturity_levels.name: Partially Connected
maturity_levels.description: Some tools connected via Zapier/Make. Basic automations running. Starting to explore AI.

maturity_levels.name: Automated
maturity_levels.description: Most tools connected. Claude Code in active use. Custom skills being built. Context OS started.

maturity_levels.name: AI-Native
maturity_levels.description: Full AIOS operational. AI embedded in every process. Skills library mature. Context OS rich. Dashboard unified.

overall_score_calculation: Sum of all 7 layer scores (each 1-10) mapped to 1-100 scale: overall = round((sum_of_layers / 70) * 100)
